quarterly_data.signal: First quarter 2026 ongoing earnings of $0.91 per share versus $0.84 per share in 2025 (GAAP $0.89 per share). CFO Brian Van Abel: higher electric revenues from rate case outcomes, non-fuel riders and sales growth added $0.23 per share and higher AFUDC added $0.10 per share, offset by $0.18 per share of higher interest charges and common equity financing (funding the infrastructure build) and $0.05 per share of higher depreciation; weather (Colorado's warmest winter on record) cut earnings by $0.09 per share.
quarterly_data.figure: ongoing EPS $0.91 per share vs $0.84 per share; GAAP $0.89 per share

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance and load growth: management reaffirmed 2026 ongoing EPS guidance of $4.04-$4.16 per share, 6%-8%+ long-term earnings growth and 9% EPS growth on average through 2030. Weather-adjusted first-quarter electric sales increased 2.8%, driven by continued oil and gas growth in SPS and broader C&I growth, and full-year 2026 weather-adjusted electric sales are still expected to increase 3%.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 EPS guidance $4.04-$4.16; weather-adjusted electric sales +2.8% in Q1, 3% expected for 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Data center load pipeline: CEO Bob Frenzel reiterated the forecast to secure 6 GW of data center load by year-end 2027 with in-service dates into the early 2030s, and said the backlog is 'a greater than 20 GW backlog' with interest across all eight states, most in the Upper Midwest. About a gigawatt is built or under construction, another (the Google transaction) is before the commissions, and Xcel expects to sign enough ESAs this year to reach a 3 GW target and another 3 GW next year; 'we expect four more gigawatts to be contracted by the end of 2027.' Large load tariffs: filed in Colorado in April with terms similar to the Google ESA and the Minnesota filing (minimum bills, termination fees, credit requirements), with Texas, New Mexico and Wisconsin filings planned.
quarterly_data.figure: 6 GW of data center load by year-end 2027; greater than 20 GW backlog

quarterly_data.signal: NextEra Energy partnership: in April Xcel reached a definitive, non-exclusive joint development agreement with NextEra Energy (from the previously announced MOU) to co-develop generation, storage and interconnections for data centers across its operating companies, delivering a balance of company-owned resources and PPAs with NextEra across wind, solar, battery storage and natural gas. Frenzel: 'We are already underway developing solutions for 2GW of new data center capacity', that 2 GW is inclusive of the 4 GW expected to be contracted by end of 2027, and 'the JDA itself is unbounded as far as I'm concerned.'
quarterly_data.figure: 2GW of new data center capacity under development with NextEra

quarterly_data.signal: Capital plan build-out: Xcel invested over $3 billion in new infrastructure in the first quarter and is executing a 2026 $14 billion capital investment plan, its most extensive ever. It now has line of sight to at least $7+ billion of the $10+ billion incremental opportunity above the $60 billion base plan, including the 765 kV Crawfish Draw to Phantom transmission line in SPS (allocated by SPP in February, in-service goal by 2031), over 1,200 MW of the generation and storage needed for the Google data center, and 800 MW of generation approved in Colorado. Nearly 500 MW of new solar and utility-scale battery storage came online in SPS and Colorado in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: over $3 billion invested in Q1; 2026 $14 billion capital plan; line of sight to $7+ billion of the $10+ billion incremental plan

quarterly_data.signal: Equipment supply lock-in: Frenzel said supply chains and qualified labor for generation, transmission and distribution will become more constrained, which is why Xcel formed alliances with GE Vernova and NextEra and strategic agreements with Tier 1 EPC firms. Asked about GE Vernova gas turbines, he said 'We have 24 gas turbines through Siemens and General Electric that are slotted and in various stages of production and delivery over the next five years', and that negotiated and framework agreements cover wind turbines, solar, breakers and high voltage transformers. Van Abel: the base plan alone develops 10 GW of generation and storage, 7 GW of it renewables.
quarterly_data.figure: 24 gas turbines slotted over the next five years; 10 GW of generation and storage in the base plan

quarterly_data.signal: Generation needs from data center load and RFP pipeline: Van Abel said the incremental pipeline includes 10 GW-12 GW of RFPs in flight, and the 3 additional gigawatts of data centers it expects to contract would need 'another, you know, 6 GW, 9 GW, 10 GW of generation.' (An analyst cited a $6 billion-$8 billion incremental capex per gigawatt framework from the deck; management referred to it as the incremental investment to serve every gigawatt of data center.) Catalysts: SPS RFP (1,500 MW-3,000 MW nameplate) filing with New Mexico later in Q2; NSP RFP (4,000+ MW renewable generation and storage by 2030) filing in Minnesota later this year; a Colorado RFP later this year; a competitive bid for SPP 765 kV lines later this year with a decision likely next year. Xcel guides to 50/50 company-owned vs PPA and won north of 75% in the last SPS RFP.
quarterly_data.figure: 10 GW-12 GW of RFPs in flight; SPS RFP 1,500 MW-3,000 MW; NSP RFP 4,000+ MW by 2030

quarterly_data.signal: Financing the build: in the first quarter Xcel issued forward contracts for over $1 billion of equity from its ATM program and an $800 million junior subordinated note (50% equity credit), which with 2025 forwards addresses over half of the $7 billion equity need in the five-year base plan; incremental capex is funded with roughly 40% equity.
quarterly_data.figure: over $1 billion ATM forwards; $800 million junior subordinated note; over half of $7 billion equity need addressed

connects_to.relationship: Regulated power supply — carbon-free generation portfolio and interconnection serving Google's Minnesota data center

contracts.signal: Frenzel detailed the Upper Midwest Google data center contract, filed with the Minnesota PUC: under a 15-year agreement Google will cover the entire cost of its service and infrastructure, including 1,900 megawatts of new wind and solar generation and long-duration storage using Form Energy's 100-hour iron-air battery. Xcel estimates the data center (close to 1 GW) will save customers $1 billion-$1.5 billion over the ESA term, about 1%-2% residential electric customer net benefit; water use is limited by Google's air-cooled design. Over 1,200 MW (two-thirds) of the needed generation and storage is counted in Xcel's incremental investment line of sight.
contracts.units: 1,900 megawatts of new wind and solar generation and long-duration storage
contracts.value: $1 billion-$1.5 billion of customer savings over the ESA term
contracts.date_signed: 15-year agreement; ESA announced on the Q4 call, details provided during the first quarter and contract filed with the Minnesota PUC
